title: A gesturing guide needs a human voice
statement: Give a gesturing on-screen guide a human voice, since in one experiment the benefit of human-like gesture held with a human voice but not with a machine voice.
example: Three experiments found that a human-voiced agent's gestures improved transfer over a static agent, and the one that compared voices found no such gain with a machine voice.
detail: The Grade 9 video-design notes report that an agent with human-like gesture, eye gaze and movement improved transfer over a static agent, but across 3 experiments only when it spoke in a human voice, not a machine voice, rated as controlled experiments from a single research programme (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/video-02-instructional-video-design.md`, lines 28-34). The same notes record that a friendly human voice beats a synthetic or machine voice (lines 38-41), and on both grounds recommend a human-recorded, conversational voice for the guide, since a machine voice both hurts learning and removes the gesture benefit if the guide is shown moving (lines 128-130). The study's own abstract is narrower than these notes: all three experiments found the gesture benefit with a human-voiced agent, and only the second compared voices, finding the benefit with a human voice but not a machine one.
against: Another study in the same research found that "an **AI-generated voice paired with an AI-generated face outperformed all other pairings, including the fully human one, on retention**" (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/video-01-ai-humans-attention.md`, line 30), and those notes advise to "prioritize voice-face realism *matching* over maximizing either one alone" (line 72). The project also records that a human voice conflicts with a standing rule: "Our rule for G3/G5 is all audio through the course TTS route" (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/VIDEO-SYNTHESIS.md`, lines 45-46).

evidence.quote: across 3 experiments, the embodiment effect held **only when the agent spoke in a human voice, not a machine voice**.
a **friendly human voice beats a synthetic/machine voice**

citations.ref: Mayer & DaPra 2012, An Embodiment Effect in Computer-Based Learning With Animated Pedagogical Agents
Xu et al. 2025, From recorded to AI-generated instructional videos
